Data Storage & External Services

Catalog data is held in an in-memory mock service or persisted through Entity Framework to SQL Server LocalDB / the Compose SQL Server service. Images use a mock service or Azure Blob Storage. Azure AD OpenID Connect is optional; Application Insights is configured for telemetry. No active message-broker workflow was found.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Autofac selects mock or production-style services from configuration.
  • Catalog persistence uses an EF6 context directly from the catalog service; there is no separate repository implementation.
  • Image storage is abstracted behind IImageService, with mock and Azure Blob implementations.

DTOs & Contracts

CatalogItem is both the catalog domain entity and the form model for create/edit requests. PaginatedItemsViewModel is the catalog listing response model. PicController.UploadImage returns an anonymous JSON contract with name and url. These models are mutable classes; no immutable records, generated OpenAPI schema, protobuf, or GraphQL schema was found. MVC JSON serialization is used for the upload response.

Communication Patterns

  • Browser requests and MVC controller-to-service calls are synchronous.
  • Catalog persistence is performed through Entity Framework and a SQL Server connection.
  • Image operations use the IImageService abstraction, selecting mock storage or Azure Blob Storage from configuration.
  • Azure AD OpenID Connect and cookie authentication are optional. Catalog administration actions are decorated with [Authorize]; the image-upload action does not have a controller-level or action-level [Authorize] attribute. With Azure AD disabled, custom middleware assigns a ClaimsIdentity to each request without validating credentials, so [Authorize] does not provide an identity check in that configuration.
  • No retry, circuit-breaker, service-discovery, API gateway, or message-broker communication policy was found in the application source.
  • The application does not enforce HTTPS in its MVC routing configuration; TLS depends on the hosting environment.
  • Compose declares the SQL dependency, but no readiness wait or database health check is configured.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining an e-commerce product catalog. Administrators can create, edit, and delete catalog items, while product images are handled separately through the configured image-storage implementation.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalog ManagementProduct offered in the catalog, with price, stock, and image referenceBelongs to one CatalogBrand and one CatalogType
CatalogBrandCatalog ManagementBrand classification for productsHas many catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalog ManagementProduct type classificationHas many catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopModernizedMVCCatalog ManagementCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeSQL Server or in-memory mock data; optional Azure Blob image storage

There are no independently deployed business services or cross-context data exchanges. The MVC application is the source of truth for catalog entities.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog index with optional page size and page index.
  2. CatalogController asks the catalog service for a sorted page of items.
  3. The service loads related brand and type data and returns pagination metadata.
  4. The controller resolves image URLs and renders the catalog view.

Workflow 2: Create or edit a catalog item

  1. An authorized user opens the create or edit form.
  2. If an image is selected, the browser posts it to the image-upload action; the handler accepts JPEG, PNG, or GIF content and returns a temporary image URL.
  3. The authorized create/edit action validates the submitted CatalogItem model.
  4. On create, the service assigns an identifier and persists the item. On edit, it updates the selected item.
  5. If a temporary image is present, the image service promotes it to the catalog item’s image location.
  6. The controller redirects to the catalog index.

Workflow 3: Delete a catalog item

  1. An authorized user reviews the item and submits the delete form.
  2. The controller loads the item, removes it through the catalog service, saves the change, and redirects to the index.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No business-service aggregation or cross-service joins were found. Catalog metadata is retrieved from the catalog store; image files use the selected mock or Azure Blob storage service. Blob operations and SQL updates are separate and do not participate in a distributed transaction. No circuit-breaker fallback behavior was found.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Admin participant Pic as "PicController" participant Image as "Image Service" participant Catalog as "CatalogController" participant Service as "Catalog Service" participant SQL as "SQL Server" participant Blob as "Azure Blob Storage" Admin->>Pic: POST /uploadimage with image alt Supported image content Pic->>Image: Upload temporary image Image->>Blob: Store image when Azure storage is enabled Blob-->>Image: Temporary image URL Image-->>Pic: Image URL Pic-->>Admin: JSON name and URL else Invalid image content Pic-->>Admin: 400 Bad Request end Admin->>Catalog: POST /Catalog/Create Catalog->>Catalog: Validate CatalogItem model alt Model is valid Catalog->>Service: Create catalog item Service->>SQL: Save catalog row SQL-->>Service: Item persisted opt Temporary image was supplied Catalog->>Image: Promote temporary image Image->>Blob: Copy image to item location Blob-->>Image: Copy accepted end Catalog-->>Admin: Redirect to catalog index else Model is invalid Catalog-->>Admin: Return create form with errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog item name is required. Price is constrained to 0–1,000,000 and at most two decimal places.
  • Available stock, restock threshold, and maximum stock threshold each have a 0–10,000,000 range.
  • Entity Framework requires each catalog item to reference an existing brand and type.
  • Create, edit, delete, and image mutation decisions are guarded by model validity and/or authorization attributes on catalog administration actions.
  • Startup seeds catalog types, brands, and items from predefined data or CSV files, depending on UseCustomizationData.
  • SQL persistence uses SaveChanges; image storage is a separate operation with no cross-resource transaction or compensation flow.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and ASP.NET MVC 5, rather than modern .NET. Several package families are legacy versions, including Microsoft.Extensions 3.0.0, older Azure client libraries, and the 5.6.0 Identity Model packages. Moving to a modern runtime will require replacing or upgrading framework-specific packages and reviewing binding redirects.

Notable Observations

  • The project uses a legacy packages.config dependency model and contains 146 package entries.
  • Redis packages are present, but the Redis session-state configuration is commented out.
  • Azure Service Bus is declared but no application-level message publishing or receiving path was identified.
  • Application Insights is represented by multiple integration and collector packages.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The catalog data model contains three EF6 entities stored in SQL Server, with an in-memory mock alternative. Entity Framework maps catalog items to required brand and type relationships.

Caching Strategy

No active application data cache was found. The mock catalog is mutable process-local state, not a cache. Redis packages are present, but the Redis session-state provider configuration in Web.config is commented out.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The MVC application owns and accesses one catalog database; no service-to-service database boundary or cross-service data aggregation exists. The mock-data option replaces SQL persistence with an in-memory list. Image files are stored separately through the image service abstraction, so SQL updates and blob operations do not share a transaction.
